headline: Officials identify all six aboard medical plane lost off Nantucket
dek: The Coast Guard named four Canadian crew members and two Bermudian passengers after suspending a 66-hour search; Canada’s Transportation Safety Board is leading the investigation.
body: The U.S. Coast Guard has identified all six people aboard a medical transport jet that disappeared on a Bermuda-to-Boston flight, a new development after the agency suspended its active search Sunday. The Coast Guard said the aircraft went missing off Nantucket early Saturday and that a civilian vessel later found debris associated with it. [CBS Boston, reporting with the Associated Press](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/nantucket-plane-sergio-wayne-lottimore-marilyn-lavonne-bean/), published the names Monday night.

The four Canadian crew members were identified as Philip Gregory Childerhose, Thomas Henry Farquhar, Sarah Jane Paton and Jolene Beth Weir. The two Bermudian passengers were Marilyn Lavonne Bean, 66, and her son, Sergio Wayne Lottimore, 41, according to CBS/AP and the [Bermuda Broadcasting Company’s report on the Coast Guard release](https://bbc.bm/?embed=&radio_player=3). The Coast Guard’s earlier [Northeast District update](https://x.com/USCGNortheast/status/2106332164568801317) identified the aircraft as a Gulfstream G100 and said it was traveling from Bermuda to Boston.

The aircraft was operated by Latitude Air Ambulance, an Ontario-based medical transport company. It departed L.F. Wade International Airport on a nighttime flight toward Boston Logan International Airport, carrying four Canadian crew members and two Bermudian passengers. The Bermuda passengers were described in earlier reporting as a patient and a family companion, but officials have not publicly clarified which of the two was receiving medical care in Boston. The company said its four crew members were presumed dead while emphasizing that it would not speculate about the cause before investigators complete their work, [AP reported](https://apnews.com/article/plane-search-bermuda-boston-nantucket-mother-son-52dd17ea4c9f5d3dab70400b54844dba).

The Coast Guard ended the active rescue effort after roughly 66 hours and a search covering more than 4,400 square miles of ocean, according to CBS/AP. Searchers found the debris field about 20 miles south of Nantucket in waters reported to be roughly 80 to 90 feet deep. The suspension ended the surface search for survivors, but it did not resolve the aircraft’s final flight path, the condition of the wreckage or the circumstances of the crash.

The response was centered on the waters south of Nantucket and involved Coast Guard aircraft, boats and cutters, Massachusetts authorities and the New York National Guard’s Air Rescue Wing. [Boston 25 News](https://www.boston25news.com/news/local/coast-guard-suspends-search-missing-medical-transfer-jet-found-off-nantucket/I4YKQH5TABGGDNWHKKDC73YEYA/?outputType=amp) reported that assets included crews from Air Station Cape Cod, Station Brant Point and the cutter William Sparling. The scale of the operation reflected the difficulty of searching a broad ocean area near the Massachusetts coast, even after debris was located.

The aircraft’s final moments remain preliminary evidence rather than a finding about the cause. Air-traffic-control audio reported by AP and CBS/AP indicates that the pilot reported electrical problems and declared an emergency as the jet approached the coast. The audio also included a controller asking whether the pilot was “coming in blind” as a storm moved through the area. Those details do not establish whether equipment failure, weather or another factor caused the loss of contact, and NorthEast News is not treating them as a conclusion.

Canada’s Transportation Safety Board is leading the investigation, with the National Transportation Safety Board expected to assist. The Coast Guard said questions about the investigation should go to the Canadian agency and noted that finding debris in the water is not unusual in an incident of this kind. The TSB has said investigators will help search for and recover aircraft evidence, a process that can produce new facts after the immediate rescue phase has ended, [AP reported](https://apnews.com/article/plane-search-bermuda-boston-nantucket-mother-son-52dd17ea4c9f5d3dab70400b54844dba).

The new identification gives families and the public a confirmed list of those aboard, while leaving major questions open. Officials have not issued a final public account of the crash sequence, and investigators have not attributed responsibility or cause. For Massachusetts, the incident remains closely tied to Nantucket and Cape Cod because the debris and the response were concentrated off the island as the Boston-bound aircraft approached the region. The next verified updates are likely to come from the transportation-safety investigation and any recovery of the aircraft.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Officials identify six aboard Nantucket medical plane
seoDescription: The Coast Guard identified all six people aboard a medical plane lost off Nantucket after suspending a 66-hour search.
